challenges.title: Can you fix the learning rate?
challenges.description: This neural network should learn XOR, but its learning rate is far too large. Train it, watch it fail, then fix the learning rate.
challenges.objective: See that a correct algorithm can still fail because of its configuration.
hints: Look at the loss curve: it rises instead of falling. Every step overshoots.
Learning rates for this network usually work between 0.05 and 1.
Try 0.3.
challenges.explanation: With learning rate 20 every update overshoots the minimum and the network saturates into confident wrong answers - the loss explodes. A smaller learning rate takes steps small enough to follow the loss surface downhill. The algorithm never changed; only its configuration did.

challenges.title: Make gradient descent diverge
challenges.description: On the bowl L = x^2 + y^2, choose a learning rate that makes every step overshoot further than the last.
challenges.objective: Connect divergence to the stability limit 2 / L''.
hints: Here L'' = 2, so the stability limit is 2 / 2.
Anything above 1.0 diverges.
challenges.explanation: For L = a x^2 each step multiplies x by (1 - 2 a eta). When |1 - 2 a eta| > 1, i.e. eta > 1/a, the distance to the minimum grows geometrically: divergence.

challenges.title: Find where oscillation begins
challenges.description: Find a learning rate at which the iterates start flipping sides of the minimum - but only just: at most 0.55.
challenges.objective: Locate the boundary between monotone convergence and oscillation.
hints: The multiplier per step is (1 - 2 eta).
It becomes negative - flipping sign - when eta > 0.5.
challenges.explanation: x is multiplied by (1 - 2 eta) each step. For eta < 0.5 the factor is positive (monotone approach); above 0.5 it is negative, so x flips sign every step while still shrinking until eta reaches 1.

challenges.title: Cross the elongated valley
challenges.description: Plain gradient descent on a stretched valley (a = 0.2, b = 4). Converge within 200 iterations.
challenges.objective: Balance the steep and flat directions with a single learning rate.
hints: The steep direction caps eta below 2 / 8 = 0.25.
Too small and the flat direction crawls. The best single rate is 2 / (lambda_min + lambda_max).
challenges.explanation: The optimal fixed rate is 2 / (0.4 + 8) = 0.238. Even then progress along the flat direction is slow: the condition number 20 governs the speed of plain gradient descent.

challenges.title: Beat the valley with momentum
challenges.description: Same valley, now with momentum. Converge within 60 iterations.
challenges.objective: See how momentum accelerates along consistent directions.
hints: Too much momentum overshoots and rings; too little is plain GD.
Heavy-ball theory suggests eta near 0.33 and beta near 0.4 for this valley.
challenges.explanation: Heavy-ball momentum effectively uses the square root of the condition number: optimal eta = 4/(sqrt(Lmax)+sqrt(Lmin))^2 and beta = ((sqrt(k)-1)/(sqrt(k)+1))^2, converging several times faster than plain GD.

challenges.title: Demonstrate underfitting
challenges.description: Configure a model too weak for concentric circles.
challenges.objective: Recognise underfitting: poor accuracy even on training data.
hints: What can a model with no hidden layer draw?
challenges.explanation: Without a hidden layer the network is logistic regression and can only draw a straight line; circles need a curved boundary.

challenges.title: Solve XOR
challenges.description: Find any configuration that reaches 95% test accuracy on XOR.
hints: XOR is not linearly separable - add a hidden layer.
Adam with learning rate ~0.03 and a hidden layer of 8 is a good start.
challenges.explanation: A hidden layer with a nonlinearity lets the network bend its decision boundary into the two diagonal regions XOR requires.

challenges.title: Overfit within 50 epochs
challenges.description: On the noisy spiral, make training accuracy pull away from test accuracy in at most 50 epochs.
challenges.objective: Understand that capacity plus noise plus no regularisation produces overfitting.
hints: Give the network far more capacity than the data supports.
Wide layers and a larger learning rate memorise fast.
challenges.explanation: A large network fits the noise in a small training set; the memorised quirks do not transfer to the test points, so the gap opens.

challenges.title: Memorise the noise
challenges.description: Make a classifier score 100% on training data while test accuracy falls far behind.
challenges.objective: Diagnose overfitting from a train/test gap.
hints: Unlimited-depth trees can memorise anything.
Corrupting labels gives them something wrong to memorise.
challenges.explanation: An unconstrained tree carves a leaf for every corrupted label. It is perfect on training data and wrong on new data.

challenges.title: Rescue k-NN
challenges.description: k-NN on wine scores poorly. Reach 95% test accuracy without changing the model.
challenges.objective: See why distance-based models need feature scaling.
hints: One wine feature (proline) is in the hundreds; others are below 1.
After scaling, also try a few values of k.
challenges.explanation: Unscaled, proline dominates every distance, so k-NN effectively uses one feature. Standardising gives every feature a voice.

challenges.title: Push macro F1 above 0.97
challenges.description: On breast cancer data, reach macro F1 of at least 0.97.
challenges.objective: Improve a balanced metric, not just accuracy.
hints: A depth-1 tree is a single question.
Try a standardised linear model or SVM.
challenges.explanation: Margin-based linear models with standardised inputs separate this dataset well; F1 rewards getting both classes right.

challenges.title: Push the answer out of first place
challenges.description: For the question 'what is the stability limit for the learning rate', the Gradient Descent lesson holds the answer and currently ranks first. Change chunking and BM25 settings until a different lesson takes rank 1.
challenges.objective: See how chunking and scoring choices put the wrong passage in front of a generator.

initial_config.query: what is the stability limit for the learning rate

target.label: Rank 1 is not the Gradient Descent lesson

hints: Very small chunks lose the context that makes a passage relevant.
Try 8-word chunks, keep stopwords, and exaggerate BM25: b = 1, k1 = 5.
challenges.explanation: Eight-word chunks cut the sentence that answers the question into fragments, while b = 1 and k1 = 5 over-reward short fragments that repeat a query word. A Linear Regression fragment wins rank 1. In a RAG system the generator would now answer from the wrong passage.

challenges.title: Sharpen retrieval
challenges.description: Reach mean reciprocal rank of at least 0.9 on the evaluation set with top_k at most 3.
challenges.objective: Tune chunking and BM25 for precise retrieval.

initial_config.query: why does a large learning rate diverge

hints: Smaller focused chunks with some overlap.
Restore length normalisation (b ~ 0.75) and drop stopwords.
challenges.explanation: Focused chunks and length normalisation put the passage that answers the question at rank 1.

challenges.title: Run out of GPU memory
challenges.description: Configure a deployment that cannot fit on its GPU.
challenges.objective: Estimate weights + KV cache against device memory.
hints: A 7B model in fp16 needs about 14 GB just for weights.
challenges.explanation: Weights scale with parameters x bytes per parameter; the KV cache scales with layers x context x hidden x batch.
